subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 40-year-old man whose diet lacks dairy products and green leafy vegetables presents with cracked, fissured lips, a magenta tongue, and corneal vascularization. Urine organic acids show increased medium-chain dicarboxylic acids, and his diet history is otherwise adequate.
question: Decreased activity of which of the following enzymes of beta-oxidation is most directly attributable to this vitamin deficiency?
explanation_correct: The findings are typical of riboflavin (vitamin B2) deficiency. Riboflavin is the precursor of FAD and FMN, and acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, the first enzyme of each beta-oxidation cycle, requires FAD to oxidize the acyl chain to a trans-enoyl-CoA; impaired activity leads to accumulation of fatty acid derivatives and dicarboxylic acids.

explanation_incorrect.B: Enoyl-CoA hydratase adds water across the double bond and requires no vitamin-derived cofactor.
explanation_incorrect.C: 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase uses NAD+, derived from niacin (vitamin B3), not riboflavin.
explanation_incorrect.D: beta-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase requires coenzyme A, derived from pantothenic acid (vitamin B5), rather than FAD.
explanation_incorrect.E: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase I is part of the carnitine shuttle and does not use a flavin cofactor.

educationalObjective: Riboflavin-derived FAD is required by acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, the first step of beta-oxidation.
